create issue (WORKING RECIPE 2026-09-10): jq's --arg/$var syntax gets falsely flagged by the sandbox's shell-expansion detector even inside single-quoted jq filters - AVOID --arg entirely. Instead: (1) Write the markdown body via the Write tool to a file INSIDE the repo working dir, e.g. eslint-factory/.tmp_issueN_body.md (jq/Bash cannot read files under /tmp/gh-aw/agent or other non-workdir paths - 'blocked' error). (2) Run `jq -Rs '{title: "literal title text", body: ., labels: ["eslint","eslint-factory"]}' eslint-factory/.tmp_issueN_body.md > eslint-factory/.tmp_issueN.json` (title as a literal string directly in the filter, NOT via --arg). (3) `safeoutputs create_issue . < eslint-factory/.tmp_issueN.json`. (4) rm both temp files after and confirm `git status --short eslint-factory/` is clean.

dedupe: gh api with query-string form WORKS: `gh api "repos/github/gh-aw/issues?state=open&per_page=100&labels=eslint-factory" --jq '.[] | {number,title}'`. The -f flag form 403s - use query-string form. To check WHY a specific issue closed: `gh api "repos/github/gh-aw/issues/NNNN" --jq '{state,state_reason,closed_at}'` and `gh api "repos/github/gh-aw/issues/NNNN/comments" --jq '.[].body'` - look for the 'automatically closed because it expired' bot comment vs a real human close.

Bash BLOCKS (expanded 2026-09-10): output redirection (`>`) to ANY path outside the repo working dir (including /tmp/gh-aw/agent) is blocked, not just listing. jq reading input files outside the repo working dir is also blocked. Any `$identifier` token in a bash command line (even inside single-quoted jq/awk filters meant for that tool, not the shell) can trip the 'shell expansion syntax requires manual approval' guard - avoid jq --arg/--argjson, prefer literal values baked into the filter string. Running a python3 script by path (`python3 script.py`) silently requires approval and never proceeds in this non-interactive context - avoid; do file construction via Write + jq only. `ls`/listing on /tmp/gh-aw/repo-memory/* via Bash is blocked - use Glob tool instead, it works fine there.
